Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 20: Tottenham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 17th

Prospects

Tottenham’s hopes for the season can be measured by what went wrong last season. And the season before that. This time last year, the arrival of a fresh, enthusiastic face in Thomas Frank gave considerable grounds for optimism. Surely Spurs would not be as bad in the Premier League as they had been in 2024-25? They proved to be worse. Despite a decent enough Champions League group stage, European football did not provide salvation for an ill-fitting manager or the unconvincing hierarchy around him.

That Frank is almost a forgotten figure owes much to the Igor Tudor interlude, a misadventure that resembled a disaster movie. Tottenham were on the brink of relegation until the season’s final days, a saga that became irresistible to rubberneckers. Roberto De Zerbi’s appointment was a much-needed corrective, the change in direction Spurs supporters clamoured for during so many years of their club never paying top dollar, of cutting corners. The Italian’s high wages were not his only demands. Fuller control than his predecessors, far more than he enjoyed at Brighton and Marseille, and a proper transfer spend on readymade players were also demanded. He has received them, though the lack of a top-level striker is glaring.

Thus, the unusual sensation of Tottenham being among the transfer window’s biggest spenders. Buying Jan Paul van Hecke, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, with Savinho and Omar Marmoush expected to also arrive from Manchester City, resembles the type of outlay rarely seen since Terry Venables was collecting Paul Gascoigne and Gary Lineker at White Hart Lane in the late 1980s or the influx of foreign talent in the mid-1990s – Jürgen Klinsmann, Ilie Dumitrescu and all that: a flash of glamour that is old-school Spurs. Andy Robertson’s addition as an experienced head is a further pointer towards a different Tottenham, one where success is expected and not promised, a very different form of optimism. Cristian Romero has departed, a player of talent whose foibles often betrayed his teammates, endemic of the Spurs era he played in.

Off-field picture

Finishing 17th two seasons in succession is bad for the bank balance. The club’s 2025 accounts revealed that the £34.7m garnered from winning the Europa League was wiped out by a £38.9m shortfall in Premier League income. Champions League football last season will help, with £71.6m trousered, but there are no European funds to feed off this season. The international break in September allows Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to welcome Jay-Z, having hosted the veteran heavy metal band System Of A Down in July. Two NFL regular season matches will be staged in October. Such revenue streams cushion Spurs, as does an August share issue that raised £100m.

Owner-fan relationship

The removal of Daniel Levy was what many Spurs fans had desired, but it also created a vacuum. The family trust of the former majority shareholder, Joe Lewis, took the residual heat. In January, Lewis’s daughter, Vivienne, was confronted by a fan demanding that Frank be sacked and that she sell up. The Lewis trust has doubled down. Levy’s 29% previous share is reduced by his missing the deadline for that August share issue; the two parties are reported to be battling over an NBA Europe franchise. Vinai Venkatesham, a chief executive who came under heavy fire, admitted in May “a complete reset” was required. Supporters will wait to gauge the success of the brave new world.

The manager

De Zerbi’s coaching is admired across the football spectrum, Pep Guardiola a confirmed fan, though breakdowns in relationships at both Brighton and Marseille offer caution. Will he be remembered solely for saving Spurs from relegation or can he offer progress in a fashion not seen since Mauricio Pochettino arrived in 2014? He has offered notes of realism to temper the excitement of the spending spree. “We need to create a clear playing style and give a soul to this team,” the Italian said in pre-season. “So many talk about ‘projects’, but very few manage to see them through.” He has been handed as blank a canvas as is available at any major club.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen João Pedro (left) and Dário Essugo (right) try to stop Spurs’ Sandro Tonali in his tracks during the 2-1 victory over Chelsea in their Sydney Cup friendly, in which Tonali opened the scoring. Photograph: Robbie Stephenson/PA

“The gaffer was Italian, I knew him,” was among the reasons Sandro Tonali offered for choosing Tottenham when a number of other suitors came calling. “I was already watching Tonali when he was playing for Brescia, my hometown club and the team I support,” explained De Zerbi. “At the age of 18, he already looked like a veteran.” With Tonali 26, Spurs have signed a peak-age player who, the season before last, was among the very best midfielders in English football, though his final season at Newcastle was mixed. A fee of £100m could not be refused.

Stat attack

Tottenham were the only club in the Premier League who overachieved their xG in attack by at least four while also underachieving by that margin or more in defence. It was up front where the biggest discrepancy occurred, with Spurs scoring 7.91 goals more than their chances implied they deserved. They might have been playing Championship football this season had this not happened.

Set for a breakthrough

Much is expected of Mikey Moore, though he is likely to go out on loan again after a season at Rangers. Antonin Kinsky was the victim of one of the horrors of the Tudor reign, subbed off after 17 minutes against Atlético Madrid, only to be trusted by the new manager as relegation was avoided. His save from Leeds’ Sean Longstaff was highly significant in the clamber to safety. Kinsky is set to be first choice this season after the departure of Guglielmo Vicario. “He forces you to believe in yourself,” said Kinsky of De Zerbi, who in turn said: “He has great personality, strong character.”

World Cup impact

Full-backs were Tottenham’s leading men in the United States. Djed Spence has departed for Inter but Pedro Porro remains, after signing a new deal amid interest from Manchester City. Porro scored twice, including in Spain’s semi-final defeat of France. As a world champion, the 26-year-old received a guard of honour on his return to his club’s training ground, having beaten the Argentina team of the now-departed Romero in the final. Among Tottenham’s nine players in North America, the new central defensive pairing of Van Hecke and Micky van de Ven was kept apart, the latter playing left-back as the Dutch disappointed.

Sports.title: Uefa and Concacaf discuss joint Nations League in latest challenge to Fifa
Sports.content:
Uefa and Concacaf have begun talks about setting up a combined Nations League tournament featuring all 96 European and North and Central American and Caribbean countries, in another direct challenge to Fifa.

The Guardian has learned that having come together to push for Gianni Infantino’s removal in the light of the World Cup sell-off controversy, the two confederations are now working on creating their own biennial tournament, which could launch as early as 2028 after the next European Championship.

Although discussions are at an early stage, it is understood the new competition would mirror the current multi-league format used for the existing Nations Leagues by Europe’s governing body and Concacaf, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football. It would be followed by a knockout phase, a final-four tournament to determine the champions.

League A would feature the top teams in Europe, including Spain, France, England and Germany, playing competitive league fixtures against the highest-ranked nations in Concacaf such as Mexico, the United States and Canada.

Uefa and Concacaf launched Nations League competitions in 2018, with the confederations staging fixtures in the same international windows, so the mechanics required to set up a joint tournament are already in place.

Under the draft plans the league phase would be played during the existing September, October and November international breaks, followed by knockout matches in March and finals in June.

As the fixtures would take place during international windows that have already been agreed, it is unclear whether the new tournament would need to be ratified by Fifa, although given the world governing body is in the midst of an existential crisis with Infantino facing a leadership challenge that may be a moot point.

With serious discussions having begun only in the last few weeks, the number of teams in each league has yet to be determined, but all 96 members of Uefa and Concacaf would be involved and much of the revenue pooled, generating significant additional income for smaller nations.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino is under pressure with Uefa and Concacaf pushing for his removal and now planning a combined Nations League tournament. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

The commercial appeal of the bigger European teams playing regular competitive matches in North America and Canada would be considerable, while there would also be major benefits for Mexico, whose football federation (FMF) is known to be frustrated by what it sees as the financial limitations of playing within Concacaf.

The FMF has held initial discussions about leaving to join the South American confederation, Conmebol, in a move that would need to be ratified by Fifa, but the prospect of lucrative matches against European opposition could lead to a change of heart.

The proposed new format would replace rather than add to existing international fixtures, while games would be played in geographic blocks to reduce travel.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) is also understood to have expressed interest in joining a global Nations League at a future date, and the competition structure being discussed would be flexible enough to accommodate them. The AFC does not currently operate a Nations League, however, so that would be a more long-term aspiration.

Uefa and Concacaf have been working together for some time, and signed a memorandum of understanding to promote greater cooperation at Fifa’s congress in Vancouver in April, but have become even more closely aligned since the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.

Both confederations have made it abundantly clear that they regard Infantino’s position as untenable as a result of his role in the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, and are working together to propose an alternative candidate to stand against him in the presidential election next March.

Uefa declined to comment, although one source with knowledge of the proposal confirmed discussions are under way.

Concacaf declined to comment directly, but highlighted the confederation’s longstanding commitment to collaboration, which has led to guest teams participating in the Concacaf Gold Cup.

A historically strong relationship with Conmebol has resulted in many South American teams taking part in the Gold Cup, as have South Africa, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Sports.title: Manchester United’s midfield rebuild leaves Carrick with no excuses
Sports.content:
Ed Woodward to MUTV in July 2015: “When people see Bastian Schweinsteiger on the teamsheet, that’s going to send some shivers down the spine.” This prediction by Manchester United’s then executive vice-president, about Louis van Gaal’s new midfield signing, proved to be badly off-target as the World Cup-winner’s career at the club proved to be a disappointment.

Two years after Woodward’s bullish statement, Schweinsteiger departed for Chicago Fire with a paltry 35 appearances and two goals for United on his CV, having been forced to train for a while with the youngsters by José Mourinho, Van Gaal’s successor. Here, in microcosm, is the story of virtually all midfield recruits by United for a generation. The hope at the club is that this trend changed this summer, with the arrivals of Youri Tielemans for £35m from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos for £48m plus £2m in add-ons, from Chelsea, with the manager, Michael Carrick, also closing in on Brighton’s Carlos Baleba for a fee in the region of £70m.

You have to go back to Carrick’s own £18m transfer from Tottenham in 2006 for the last elite-level midfielder bought by United, who arrived with his peak years ahead of him and went on to be a consistent force for many years, a strange dereliction of duty for a lineage that boasts Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, Paul Ince, Bryan Robson, Nobby Stiles, alongside other A-list acts.

Since Carrick, Paul Pogba purchased by Mourinho a decade later for a club-record £93.2m possessed the highest ceiling, but the Frenchman was unable to return even seven or eight-out-of-10 displays in most games. Casemiro, who departed Old Trafford in May, came from Real Madrid in 2022 as a five-times Champions League-winner but, at 30, his best years were firmly behind him, and of his four years at United, only the first and last could be rated as high level.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United have been linked with a £70m swoop for the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Photograph: Jeff Mood/ProSports/Shutterstock

Cite any other signing who has patrolled United’s midfield since Carrick and you are naming mediocrity in a United shirt, at best: Fred, Morgan Schneiderlin, Ander Herrera, Sofyan Amrabat, Daley Blind and Manuel Ugarte among those on that list. The exception is a home-reared player – Kobbie Mainoo. And even a teenager who scored the winner in United’s 2024 FA Cup final triumph against Manchester City and started England’s 2-1 Euro final loss by Spain that summer, was discarded by Ruben Amorim before Carrick’s mid-January appointment, after the Portuguese’s sacking, saved his United career.

So we arrive at the start of a new campaign and Carrick’s move to end this poor engine-room policy reaches Baleba. If the 22-year-old is acquired, he will join Santos, another No 6, and Tielemans, a No 8 who will compete with Mainoo, in a central cadre that has legs, skill, aggression and knowhow. Mason Mount has also shown to be a another viable midfield option during pre-season. The 27-year-old operated with accomplishment as an attacking midfielder before sustaining his latest injury in the draw with Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

It is the latest setback for Mount, but Carrick has brushed aside any concerns regarding his robustness. “First of all Mason is a top player – we have seen that he was one of our best players in the first games,” the manager said. “He was outstanding and has picked up a bit of a knock. But there are no dramas. He has missed some football over recent years and he wants to be fit and be in full rhythm and we want to help him. Mason will be back soon.”

United travel to Hull on Saturday before hosting Ipswich a week on Sunday. Games against two newly promoted teams represent a favourable launch to Carrick’s first full campaign in charge, albeit he branded as “ridiculous” the view that it was an easy start. Yet factor in how a trip to Everton is United’s third game before Manchester City arrive at Old Trafford on 13 September and this is undoubtedly a golden chance for United to plant a flag as a potential title contender.

Reviving United amid the chaos of Amorim’s departure and finishing third last year was a fine effort by Carrick. Yet when he took over, the team were already out of both domestic cups and not in Europe. That left 17 games for the then caretaker to navigate. Now Carrick has a full programme of Premier League, Champions League, Carabao Cup and FA Cup fixture before him: a litmus test of his side, as well as of the 45-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A squad with the requisite depth of quality is beginning to form. If Baleba is added alongside a left-back – Newcastle’s Lewis Hall and Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly remain on the radar – by 1 September, then Carrick will have been bolstered by four new major transfers. There remains question marks regarding the centre-back unit but ultimately the manager can have no excuses.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick has had a lot to think about this summer. Photograph: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/Shutterstock

Of Hull being an unknown quantity, Carrick said: “That is the beauty of the new season, for teams coming up there tend to be a few changes, that is the challenge playing against them – we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work”. The last comment applies especially to the surgery undertaken to United’s midfield. At 12.30pm on Saturday, at the MKM Stadium, the picture of how good this has been will begin to emerge.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Swapped pair face former clubs

Neither Everton nor Crystal Palace have enjoyed a particularly scintillating summer of transfer activity but combined to make headlines with a swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson. The pair will face one another – and their former clubs - on the first weekend of the season, eager to prove what their worth to their new teams. McNeil was rarely a regular on Merseyside but had a positive second half to last season, ironically after a move to Crystal Palace fell through at the last minute. Johnson did not settle at Selhurst Park, unable to crack the code that would get him into the starting lineup on a weekly basis, after moving from Spurs. A fresh start should reinvigorate the duo and there is no better way to further boost the mood than beating a former employer. WU

Everton v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm

4 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

5 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

6 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

8 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

9 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s Rachel Daly: ‘It’s given me more of a focus: club football is my one job’
Sports.content:
A year after taking up golf, Rachel Daly has already reached a handicap of 19. “I think that’s too generous, I was playing really well in the summer,” she point outs before politely declaring that further questions about her pastimes are out of bounds. “I’m not that exciting, to be honest,” Daly says. “I walk the dogs, play golf. I don’t do a whole lot. I don’t lead a very exciting life.” Instead, Daly wants to talk about the new Women’s Super League season, which is more than fair enough.

Coincidentally, by next summer, 19 will be the number of seasons Daly has played at the top level, ever since breaking into Leeds’ first team as a 16-year-old in 2008, and therefore it feels reasonable to disagree with her view that a former Olympian, who played 84 times for England and was the WSL’s player of the season just three years ago, does not lead an exciting life. Yet there is another number on Daly’s mind as she discusses her role as Aston Villa’s captain.

“I’m the oldest in the team by a country mile,” the 34-year-old says, sitting down at Aston Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, where she trains alongside 20-year-olds such as Georgia Mullett and Mia McAulay, a summer signing from Rangers. “A lot of the youngsters look up to me. It’s a nice feeling. It shows that they respect me and they value me, which is nice. And equally so do I [respect them]. I’m kind of a person that believes everyone should have a voice in the building. If I can reflect that to the wider group, then they can feel comfortable being able to communicate.

“I like to hear their experiences. It’s very different from when I was at their age, how I was experiencing football. They’re all very privileged where they’re at right now. When I was younger, we were paying to play, we were in men’s kits, the whole stereotypes and all that, but it’s true, that’s exactly what was happening. I try to give them my perspective of where I was at their age. I think it helps them a little bit to understand where the game has come from. They’re a really good bunch.”

Daly is now heading into her fifth season at Villa, having arrived there from Houston Dash shortly after starting every game of England’s triumphant 2022 Euros campaign. She had spent six years with the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) side and clearly likes being settled. “I like to set my roots at places. I don’t like to jump about. I [like] that familiarity of being at the same place. Villa has a big place in my heart.

“I said when I first signed here that I wanted to be part of the journey. I’ve stayed and been part of that journey and seen how we’ve moved and how we’ve progressed. I like to commit to a club and see what I can do there and give it my all. I’m really happy to be here and it feels like home.”

View image in fullscreen Rachel Daly has a leadership role at Aston Villa and is the club captain. Photograph: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

During her time at Villa, Daly also helped England reach a World Cup final in Sydney in 2023, before announcing her retirement from international football the following April. That meant her watching 2025’s Euros triumph, including the tense drama of penalties, as a nervous fan. “It’s awful actually, I much prefer playing than watching,” Daly admits. “I was just like, ‘just win, please!’”. Reflecting on her decision to call time on her Lionesses career, having scored 16 senior international goals, Daly says: “I made that decision purely for me. I needed to do that at the time of my life. For club football, it’s given me more of a focus: ‘That’s my one job’. Recovery-wise, obviously, I’m not getting any younger, so it gave me more time, I got my international breaks back. It’s about spending time with my family. I didn’t want to miss out on my nephew growing up and stuff like that. So it was the right decision at the right time for me.”

“I do think I feel fresher,” Daly adds. “It’s taxing on your body being away for 10 days every month. Getting that time back and mentally just resetting – the most positive thing I’ve felt is just being able to breathe and get that time back with my family. I missed a lot of [family] time when I was in America.” Asked how she likes to use her free time during international breaks now, she says: “Because of the demands of being a professional footballer and the environment you’re in, it’s nice to just do nothing. I like what I like. It’s just been nice to kick back and just chill a little bit.”

On the pitch, Daly is determined to do the exact opposite and has a laser-like focus on ensuring Villa improve on last season’s ninth place. “We weren’t happy with the way we finished,” she says, recalling Villa’s run of four straight defeats at the end of the campaign. “There’s no denying that it’s the best league in the world for a reason and it’s not just us that are investing. There are a lot of clubs investing. We need to improve on where we finished last year. And for us, it’s kind of a bit of a transition, rebuilding year. There’s a lot of big players that left last year and there’s a lot of new faces in the door. A lot of young players, which is exciting. But [the aim] is building on how we left last year.”

The WSL is entering a new phase of its development, with two extra teams entering the league this season. “It excites me,” Daly says. “The league has been kind of at a steady place for quite a while but we need growth, we need change, we need to have more teams in the league, we need to expand. And I think it came at a really good time. There’s no downside to it. More games means more fun.”

View image in fullscreen Rachel Daly has scored 16 times for England and was part of the Euro 2022-winning side. Photograph: Nigel Keene/ProSports/Shutterstock

The first two games of Villa’s campaign look tricky; away to Chelsea on 5 September before hosting Manchester City, the defending champions, eight days later. “Yes, September will be tough, starting against Chelsea and City is not an easy feat,” Daly says, who has never played at Stamford Bridge. “It’ll be a good test for us. We’re in a good spot so it will be interesting to see how that month goes, but I back us all the time. If you want to be the best, you’ve got to play the best and I think there’s no better place to start than playing Chelsea.”

Villa’s last trip to Chelsea in March ended in a seven-goal thriller. If anything similar occurs this time around, the WSL campaign will be off to a roaring start. “It’s exciting,” Daly says. “Big hitters early doors. Lets see what happens.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace agree Disasi loan and tell Manchester City that Wharton is not for sale
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign Axel Disasi on loan and are expecting further interest in some of their key players in the final week of the transfer window, having informed Manchester City that Adam Wharton is not for sale.

Palace have been searching for a replacement for Maxence Lacroix after selling the France defender to Chelsea and are also understood to have approached Xabi Alonso’s side over a potential move for Josh Acheampong. But with Chelsea not willing to allow the England Under-21s international to leave Stamford Bridge, Palace have opted to bring in Disasi instead. The 28-year-old, who spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham, is set to complete his medical on Friday.

Palace are also hoping to bring in a midfielder before the deadline and have expressed an interest in signing Kévin Danois from Auxerre and Monaco’s Lamine Camara. But it is understood the Conference League winners are determined to keep Wharton after City made an inquiry about the England midfielder this week. The 22-year-old has three years left on his contract at Selhurst Park and it is thought Palace would demand a sizeable fee to consider selling him. Liverpool and Chelsea have both also shown interest in Wharton in the past, with the latter said to be monitoring his situation should City make a bid for Enzo Fernández.

Pierre Sage is hoping Wharton will stay for another season. “We sold big players and now I think it’s not the moment to do that,” said Palace’s manager as he prepared for their Premier League opener against Everton on Saturday. “Adam can play at a big club but I think one year with us, one year with a new dynamic, will be good for him and we need him.”

Sage delivered the same message about Ismaïla Sarr after Palace turned down a bid of about £26m from Galatasaray for the Senegal forward. The Turkish side are expected to return with an improved offer and could face competition from their Istanbul rivals Fenerbache for last season’s top scorer. “We will keep him,” said Sage. “He’s a really important player for the club and for us. He will be able to play this weekend.”

There is, however, a strong possibility that Daniel Muñoz could depart after Palace signed Anan Khalaili last week, and given his fellow new recruits Óscar Mingueza and Zavier Gozo can also fill the right-wingback role. The Colombia defender has entered the final two years of his contract and is thought to be valued at about £25m, with Everton, Nottingham Forest and Tottenham having been linked with him in recent days.

Sports.title: Jovial Jakirovic determined to haul Hull over and beyond Coles’ relegation jibes
Sports.content:
On a baking spring bank holiday, Sergej Jakirovic basked in the glory of Hull’s fairytale promotion to the Premier League in an address to 40,000 ecstatic supporters from the balcony of Hull City Hall. “I only had one task before the season – to stay in the Championship … I failed. We’re going to the Premier League!” roared the Jakirovic to the delight of those in attendance.

Oli McBurnie’s late goal had secured a 1-0 win over Middlesbrough in the Championship playoff final 48 hours earlier, clinching one of the unlikeliest ascents for years. Hull only survived relegation to League One on goal difference in 2024-25 but Jakirovic, an intriguing character and fine raconteur, proved the man with the alchemist’s touch.

Three months on from those wild celebrations, the Bosnians new-look side must defy the odds again – and then some – to survive in the Premier League. Hull have been written off as relegation certainties by bookmakers and pundits, including former England duo Carlton Cole and Joe Cole, who ridiculed them on their podcast this week. “Hull are gone, man,” said the latter. “They have spent £70m and I’d be stunned if they stay up. They have come in through the back door, they’ve slipped in.”

Such barbs do not faze Hull’s head coach, who was in typically ebullient mood before Manchester United’s visit to the MKM Stadium on Saturday lunchtime. “I’m buzzing,” said the 49-year-old. “Of course there’s a very big gap between the Championship and Premier League. We’re up against the best teams, players and managers and I’ve seen all the predictions. But it’s a great motivation to prove them wrong because we don’t have anything to lose.

“What we did last season was a very big achievement, but this is football and what happened yesterday doesn’t matter any more. We want to improve and show that we can develop to do even better as a team – and of course we need another miracle to survive. It will be an even bigger achievement than winning promotion if we manage to stay up. We need 40 points, so everything is very clear.”

View image in fullscreen Jens Hjertø-Dahl, one of Hull’s new arrivals, heads at the Nice goal during last Saturday’s pre-season friendly. Photograph: Richard Bierton/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

Jakirovic has made the people of Hull walk a little taller in a city which has received more than its fair – or rather, unfair – share of negative publicity at times. What did he make of the jibes from both Coles, which provoked such a furious backlash from Tigers fans? “It was stupid and disrespectful towards the club and players because we earned everything on the pitch – nobody gave us anything for free,” said Jakirovic. “It’s not fair, especially when it’s coming from ex-players who know how hard players work to reach the Premier League. If they were in my position they would fight, so it’s easy to say we’ll finish 20th, but can they bet on that? They can put everything on that or they can lose, so we will see. But we’re not here by accident.”

The club’s high-profile chairman Acun Ilicali, who has said he will keep faith with Jakirovic even if Hull go down, has made 11 new signings – several of whom are currently injured – and broken the club’s transfer record twice in the process. The recruitment drive, described by some as scattergun, is also not over “We’re expecting three or four more players,” Jakirovic said. “We’ve signed some good players with potential, but I’m also aware that they need more time to adapt and build chemistry with the team.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Mr Chairman and I have had a very good connection since our first meeting and we do everything together. In all decisions, we are always speaking and trying to improve our team in many ways.”

Hull’s dramatic rise last season – their fourth promotion to the Premier League from 2008 onwards – caught the imagination, and Jakirovic is a good story in his own right. Born in Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina, then part of Yugoslavia, the imposing former centre-half grew up in Metkovic in Croatia. His childhood experiences – running from fighter plane bombings and taking shelter during the 1990s Balkan wars – deeply shaped his resilience and perspective on life.

Jakirovic’s playing career included spells in Slovakia, Slovenia and Bulgaria before he moved into management and eventually landed in Hull – his eighth club in nine years – last summer. “I always sleep like a baby because this is just sport at the end of the day,” he said with a smile. “I have to be fresh on Saturday; I also need to show my potential and prove that I can handle this stage. And I don’t have any doubt because I’ve showed already that I’m capable of doing some great things.”

Sports.title: Fulham summer signing could be Alvaro Arbeloa’s legacy – even if he gets sacked
Sports.content:
Fulham summer signing could be Alvaro Arbeloa’s legacy – even if he gets sacked

Alvaro Arbeloa's biggest contribution at Fulham could be signing Gonzalo Garcia - he can be a shining light this season.

That's according to talkSPORT's Kevin Hatchard, who has tipped the Cottagers' summer signing from Real Madrid to make his mark in English football regardless of how new boss Arbeloa fares.



5 Gonzalo Garcia has a chance to become a Premier League star at Fulham Credit: Getty

A new era has begun at Craven Cottage after Arbeloa was named as Marco Silva's successor on a three-year deal.

It marked an immediate return to management for the Spaniard, who was replaced by Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid in June.

The appointment has left some scratching their heads, with Arbeloa's first-ever senior coaching stint resulting in a rare trophyless season at the Santiago Bernabeu last term - making him an early sack candidate in the Premier League ahead of the season.



Fulham's saviour?

Looking to prove his doubters wrong, one of Arbeloa's first moves as Fulham boss was snapping up former player Garcia from Real.

The 22-year-old signed a five-year deal with the Cottagers for a reported fee of £34million after a breakthrough year in the Spanish capital under his old coach.



After finishing as joint-top scorer in last summer's Club World Cup with four goals, Garcia went on to notch eight times in 39 appearances overall in the 2025/26 season, earning the trust of former youth team coach Arbeloa.

And Hatchard believes the young Spaniard has the potential to shine for Fulham, highlighting his impressive exploits at Real Madrid.



Hatchard told the talkSPORT Daily Podcast: “What I really like about him is the work rate and the competitive instincts.

"Coaches would say, even in pickup games, like kickabouts, he'd be a nightmare because he'd treat them like a Champions League final - he just never wants to lose anything.

"His rise has been very impressive. And Arbeloa was a central figure in that because he was in charge of the youth sides and he gave Garcia plenty of game time.

5 Alvaro Arbeloa is beginning just his second senior managerial role at Fulham Credit: Getty



5 Garcia was a success story in a difficult spell as Real Madrid boss for Arbeloa Credit: Getty

“Garcia rewarded him by scoring loads of goals, and then it was Xabi Alonso that opened the door for him at the Club World Cup.

“And nobody expected him to play much, certainly nobody expected him to score much, but Kylian Mbappe got gastroenteritis - it worked really well for him.

“So he really stepped into the void and stepped into the limelight and he was joint top scorer in that Club World Cup by the time it finished."



Reservations

Hailing Garcia's versatility, Hatchard conceded the one thing that could hold him back is a potentially difficult season collectively.

With Arbeloa's lack of managerial experience and success coming under scrutiny, Fulham have been tipped to struggle - even being named as outside relegation candidates - especially after losing a number of key senior figures.

Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez both left as free agents, while Issa Diop moved to newly-promoted Ipswich in an £8.5m deal.

5 Garcia's first competitive outing in a Fulham shirt will come against Chelsea in their Premier League opener Credit: Getty



On Garcia, Hatchard continued: “He's somebody that isn't necessarily always a straight No.9. He can play wide. He's got pace. He can link. He can run in behind. Very smart young footballer.

“My only concern is that I think Fulham are going to struggle in general.”

While Hatchard had reservations about how Arbeloa will fare in west London, he insisted Garcia can be a positive long-term investment.

He explained: “I think even if Arbeloa is sacked mid-season, as we both suspect might end up being the case, it might end up being the best thing Arbeloa did for the club because they've brought in a guy that I think has real potential.



“Service is obviously going to be a thing. So we'll see how that works out, but he can play in multiple roles.

“He's got a real life goal and what I admire is that he came into that Club World Cup playing with some real superstars - didn't faze him at all.

5 Garcia even started ahead of Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe at times last term Credit: Getty

He praised Garcia for looking unfazed when lining up alongside Real Madrid's team of superstars, which includes the likes of Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior.



Rounding off, Hatchard said: "He looked as though he played there for ages [at Real Madrid].

“So again, there's going to be that adaptation to the Premier League, the pace and the physicality of that, but there's a lot to like, and he is desperate to learn, improve, really catch the eye.

“So I think this is something that Arbeloa has done that is really, really positive. He's been able to get a guy of that quality into Fulham.”

Sports.title: Hull owner gives furious response to viral Joe Cole and Carlton Cole video
Sports.content:
Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has hit back after a clip of Joe Cole and Carlton Cole laughing at his club went viral.

The newly-promoted Tigers host Manchester United on Saturday to mark their return to the Premier League.

3 The owner took to X to say: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better' Credit: Getty

Speaking on the 'Dressing Room' podcast, ex-England star Joe Cole claimed Hull are 'gone' before kicking a ball, sending Carlton Cole into fits of laughter.

Joe Cole then claimed he intentionally ignored a request from TNT Sports to cover the lunchtime clash - which is also live on talkSPORT.

He said: "I want to make a confession here today, right. TNT Sports have contacted me for the new season. They’ve tried to slip in the Hull one on the first day of the season. I put my phone on do not disturb!"

He added that he expects the East Yorkshire side to be in danger of relegation: "They’ve spent 70million, I’ll be stunned if they stay up. They’ve come here through the back door, they’ve slipped in."

"Lacking intelligence"

Ilicali joined talkSPORT on Friday to share his thoughts on the viral video - and he was not amused.

The businessman said: "We deserve respect, but respect can only be given by people who hold a level of intelligence, so I think there was a lack of intelligence.

"This is not a small thing. I've been all around the world, and if you ask me where I satisfy my soul, I would say, 'Hull'.

"I think this a beautiful place. Everywhere is green, and the people are beautiful.

"For me, in this conversation, they are imagining what Hull is like, which is very dangerous, and I am sure they are sorry for that. One of them tried to apologise, but this wasn't an apology.

"If someone makes fun of my mother, and then after they say, 'it was just a joke'. I can't say what I want to [because he's on-air].

3 The MKM Stadium has not hosted a Premier League game since 2017 Credit: Getty

"So, they have to be careful when they talk about topics like this."

"It's just banter"

Carlton Cole, who hosts our Sports Bar Weekender on Friday nights, insisted the clip was being taken too seriously.

Taking to Instagram, he said: "We've come under a bit of fire at the Dressing Room. The Hull City fans are not happy with us.

"Listen, a bit of back and forth, a bit of banter, it's alright. It's not the end of the world. One man's opinion doesn't make it right, doesn't make it real.

"You might be disappointed with that opinion, but it's alright. That's the whole point of football. Yes, I did belly laugh when he said that you snuck in at the back door. I did. Come on, it's funny. I'm laughing at my mate's joke. I can do that.

"Joe thinks that you won't stay up and it's alright if you don't stay up. It's okay. You've done well to get to this point.

"I love Hull City. I've got admiration for Hull City. My son was there. He's now at Middlesbrough, but when I look back, the fans were amazing.

He added: "So what I want from you is to suggest a forfeit. If you do stay up, or anybody that thinks Hull's going to stay up, send your suggestions in for a forfeit for Joe Cole."

Embracing the 'underdog' status

Last season, the Tigers were widely tipped to suffer relegation to League One; however, they defied the odds to win the Championship play-off final amid the controversy around 'Spygate'.

Despite securing promotion, many pundits have immediately tipped Hull City for a swift return to the second tier.

However, Ilicali believes manager Sergej Javorcic and his players will revel in the role of being the Premier League's underdogs.

He added: "This is such a normal thing. I checked 25, maybe 30 predictions and all of them put us first to go down.

3 Hull won the play-offs after the Spygate drama between Middlesbrough and Southampton Credit: Getty

"But just check who was the favourite to be relegated last year in the Championship and we got promoted, so this only makes us laugh, we like to be called the underdogs.

"For us, we will bring five or six new players in next week, so the team that will be on the pitch [this Saturday] will not remain the team all season.

"We are never afraid, and these players have made us so proud, so many times. For us, I'm hopeful and I believe in my boys and I'm sure they're going to do us proud again."

Hull have brought in a raft of new players, and there are more expected in the final days of the window.

They have only lost one game over pre-season, which was against Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt.

However, the squad has suffered numerous injury blows, including new signing Jack Butland, with the former England international goalkeeper expected to be sidelined until Christmas.

Nevertheless, Hull will hope that with the new additions of Nobel Mendy, Konstantinos Tzolakis and 18-year-old Aussie centre-back Lucas Herrington will help secure Premier League survival.

Sports.title: Premier League rivals warned Brentford are ‘ahead of the curve’ after signing award-winning star
Sports.content:
Premier League rivals warned Brentford are ‘ahead of the curve’ after signing award-winning star

Mamadou Sangare's arrival at Brentford shows they mean business - this is a signing a 'Champions League contender would usually make'.

That's according to talkSPORT's Kevin Hatchard, who has highlighted the Bees' impressive summer business after they pulled off the signing of highly-rated prospect Sangare.

5 Sangare got on the scoresheet as Brentford thumped Eintracht Frankfurt 7-0 in their final pre-season friendly Credit: Getty

The Mali international moved to west London for a club record fee from RC Lens after a standout debut season in Ligue 1.

While the exact figure was undisclosed, Brentford said it surpasses the £42.5m paid to sign Dango Ouattara from Bournemouth in 2025.

It's a move that has caught the eye of many, with Sangare turning down the prospect of Champions League football with Lens, as well as interest from top clubs - including Manchester United and Chelsea.

And it isn't hard to see why, with his growing reputation coming after he played a major role in Lens' second-place Ligue 1 finish last term.

Having also helped guide Les Sang et Or to Coupe de France glory, Sangare was subsequently named in Ligue 1's Team of the Year, ahead of Champions League-winning Paris Saint-Germain duo Joao Neves and Fabian Ruiz.

Big statement

Now gearing up for Brentford's Premier League opener against Tottenham on Saturday, Sangare could be just the man to transform them from European contenders to qualifiers this season.

Tipped for relegation ahead of the 2025/26 campaign after losing influential head coach Thomas Frank last summer, the Bees instead narrowly missed out European qualification on the final day, but have been backed to go one better this year.

And according to Hatchard, Keith Andrews' side mean business with Sangare in their ranks, as he outlined what he will bring to the table.

Discussing the signing on the talkSPORT Daily podcast, Hatchard began: “I think it tells you a lot because this is the guy that was one of the best players in Ligue 1 last season.

“Sangare produced some amazing midfield displays himself last season. He was in that Ligue 1 Team of the Year on merit.

5 Sangare joined Lens from Rapid Vienna last summer, and adapted to Ligue 1 football with ease Credit: Getty

5 Keith Andrews is bidding to build on Brentford's ninth-place finish last term with Sangare in his ranks Credit: Getty

“They were extraordinary last season - Lens, to push PSG all the way in the title race was phenomenal. But then to also win the Coupe de France was crazy.”

Brentford have long been known for unearthing hidden gems and developing them into elite talent - namely signing Bryan Mbeumo whilst still in the Championship in 2019, as well as discovering last season's 22-goal striker Igor Thiago.

But Hatchard believes Sangare's arrival could be their biggest move yet, who he insisted is good enough to play for Europe's elite.

A defensive midfielder capable of getting forward too, the Mali star ranked first in Ligue 1 for tackles won and possession won in the middle third, as well as scoring three goals in 29 league outings.

Hatchard continued: “Physically, I think he'll really fit what Brentford do. He'll fit the Premier League.

“And I think this is the kind of signing that a club in Europe or a Champions League contender would usually make.

5 Sangare starred as Lens won the Coupe de France for the first time in their history last season

“And I think it shows the power of the Premier League because if he rocked up at Milan or Atletico Madrid or Dortmund, you wouldn't bat an eyelid. That's the kind of signing a club like that would make.

“The fact that Brentford have been able to bring in somebody like Sangare tells you a lot - A. about the power of the Premier League and B. about how Brentford have made real leaps forward and are really trusted, I think."

'So much to like'

Continuing to hail Sangare as a major coup, Hatchard likened his arrival to Brentford's signing of Michael Kayode in 2025.

Known for his lethal long-throw deliveries, the highly-rated Italian footballer has developed into one of the Premier League's standout full-backs and was nominated for last season's Young Player of the Year award.

On Sangare, Hatchard said: “I might come unstuck here, but I genuinely can't see how it goes wrong because there's so much to like about his game.

“I think they're not the same player at all, but I was so impressed with the way they got Kayode and developed him.

5 Michael Kayode has earned a host of admirers since joining Brentford last January Credit: Getty

“I think they are totally different positions, totally different players, but the way that they brought in a guy there that had edges to smooth, but you knew had something and got him ahead of plenty of other clubs.

“This feels similar in the fact that it feels like they're ahead of the curve here.”

Outlining why Sangare is the perfect signing, Hatchard added: “He's box to box. He can give you a bit of everything, really.

"He's got that ability to break up attacks, but he's always looking to get forward, play forward, be positive.

"And I think that will really suit Brentford because one of the things that they rely upon is set plays. There's nothing wrong with that.

"What do you need for that? You need to get up the pitch and he will help them get up the pitch. So a little bit like Manzambi at Villa, that ability to carry the ball, that ability to really drive, draw contact and draw free kicks.

Sports.title: FA accused of ‘chess move’ with ‘disgraceful’ and unprecedented ban for handball
Sports.content:
FA accused of ‘chess move’ with ‘disgraceful’ and unprecedented ban for handball

The FA's decision to retrospectively ban Aune Heggebo following his handball is a 'power play' by the governing body to implement VAR.

Heggebo scored a goal with his hand during West Brom's 2-1 win over Norwich City last weekend.

3 Heggebo will miss West Brom's matches against Burnley and Newcastle Credit: Getty

However, the FA handed the Norwegian a two-match suspension for 'successfully deceive a match official by handling the ball in a direct successful attempt to score a goal'.

The Baggies unsuccessfully appealed the decision, meaning the 25-year-old will miss this weekend's league meeting with Burnley, live on talkSPORT 2, and the midweek Carabao Cup clash with Newcastle United.

One caller on Friday's talkSPORT Breakfast, however, believes Heggebo's ban is a ploy by the FA to bring VAR into the Championship.

Unlike the Premier League, clubs in the EFL, who overlook the Championship, League One and League Two, voted against implementing the Video Assistant Referee.

'Look at the bigger picture'

That may change soon, however, should the caller's suggestion come to fruition.

"People have got to look at the bigger picture. This is a massive chess move," West Ham fan, Ian, told Alan Brazil and Ray Parlour.

"The Championship clubs voted against it [VAR].

"Every deliberate dive, every deliberate shirt pull. They're all an attempt at deception of the referee.

"You can't change the narrative depending on whether the match officials see it or not.

3 VAR isn't used in the Championship after clubs voted against its implementation Credit: Getty

"To ban a player for two games, they will turn around and say: 'Well if you had VAR, that would have been picked up in the booth and you wouldn't be looking at a two-game ban'.

"So for me, this is just a power play towards trying to influence people to think that VAR should be a good thing for the Championship.

"They need to see through it."

'Disgraceful decision'

Brazil and Parlour were later joined on the show by a West Brom fan, who was in uproar about the decision to ban Heggebo.

"I think it's a disgraceful decision to be giving a player a two match ban for something the referee has missed," Baggies supporter Jordan told the pair.

"I don't think that should resort in going to VAR, to be honest.

3 The decision to ban Heggebo will 'open a can of worms' claims Parlour Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"The referees just need to be better.

"They can't be handing out players two match bans for something that they've missed."

Parlour believes this decision will open a 'can of worms' in the Championship, adding: "Totally right. There's going to be loads of incidents now in the Championship, isn't there? Loads and loads of incidents."

West Brom's welcome of Burnley kicks off at 12pm on Sunday 23 August.

What has the FA said?

Confirming the punishment in a statement, the FA spokesperson said: "West Bromwich Albion’s Aune Heggebo has been given a two-match ban for successful deception of a match official during their EFL Championship match against Norwich City on Saturday 15 August.

"It was alleged that the player acted in an improper manner in or around the 75th minute of the match, whereby he successfully deceived a match official by handling the ball in a direct and successful attempt to score a goal, contrary to FA Rule E3.1.

"Aune Heggebo denied the charge against him, however an independent Regulatory Commission found it to be proven and imposed this sanction following a hearing.

"The Regulatory Commission’s written reasons will be published in due course."

Sports.title: Aaron Wan-Bissaka seals immediate Premier League return after West Ham relegation
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have confirmed the loan signing of Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham.

Wan-Bissaka, who represented DR Congo at the 2026 World Cup, was one of a number of Hammers stars linked with a summer exit following their relegation.



3 Wan-Bissaka has joined Villa on a season-long loan with a conditional obligation to buy Credit: Official Aston Villa

Mateus Fernandes departed for rivals Tottenham, while winger Crysencio Summerville secured a big-money switch to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

And right-back Wan-Bissaka has followed the duo out of the London Stadium exit.

"Aston Villa is delighted to announce the signing of Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham United," a statement read on the club's official website.



"The DR Congo international, who played for his country at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, has joined on a season-long loan, with a conditional obligation to buy.

"A graduate of the youth academy at Crystal Palace, the 28-year-old full back would go on to spend five years at Manchester United, where he lifted the FA Cup and the EFL Cup.



"After making nearly 200 appearances at Old Trafford, he has spent the past two seasons in east London.

"Welcome, Aaron!"

Aston Villa's indifferent summer

Villa have endured a testing summer following their Europa League success last season.



Amadou Onana suffered a season-ending ACL injury with Belgium at the World Cup earlier this summer.

3 Villa were forced to sell star midfielder Tielemans this summer Credit: Getty

Compatriot Youri Tielemans then completed a shock £35million move to Manchester United, a move that talkSPORT co-host Jason Cundy has questioned.

Centre-back star Ezri Konsa is also on the cusp of a high-profile move to Arsenal, with Tosin Adarabioyo and Taylor Harwood-Bellis among those mooted to replace the England star.

Villa have added bodies to the squad, with Joao Gomes joining from Midlands rivals Wolves.

Alejandro Garnacho has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea, while Zion Suzuki will replace Emiliano Martinez between the sticks at Villa Park following his arrival from Parma.

3 Garnacho joined Villa on loan to replace Rogers following his big-money move to Chelsea Credit: Getty



Italian left-back Matteo Ruggeri also completed a move to Villa Park, the defender replacing Lucas Digne after the France international returned to Parisian powerhouse PSG.

Villa get their 2026/27 Premier League season underway on Sunday when they make the trip to Brighton.

And Wan-Bissaka is in line to make his debut for the Villans having joined before the 12pm squad registration deadline on Saturday 21 August.

Sports.title: Countdown rule introduced to Premier League and could see opposing team awarded a corner
Sports.content:
Countdown rule introduced to Premier League and could see opposing team awarded a corner

As top-flight action returns, the PGMOL has confirmed a brand-new 'five-second' restart rule that could directly hand opposition teams goal-scoring opportunities.

Ahead of the new Premier League season, the Football Association confirmed several key updates to the 'Laws of the Game'.

3 The new anti-time-wasting rules significantly reduced delays at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Referees have made it their goal to speed up effective playing time, targeting deliberate delays over goal-kicks and throw-ins.

One of the most dramatic additions is a strict five-second countdown for set-piece restarts, featuring an immediate possession reversal if the time limit is exceeded.

Handing away throw-ins or conceding cheap corners could prove disastrous for teams trying to close out tight matches.

What is the Premier League's five-second restart rule?

Under the new law, match officials will actively initiate a five-second countdown whenever a player is deemed to be unnecessarily delaying the taking of a throw-in or goal-kick.

Referees will begin counting after using an arm motion to signal the countdown if players take too long to retrieve the ball or deliberately waste time positioning it.

If play is not restarted before the countdown finishes, the referee will enforce an immediate penalty.

For throw-ins, possession is forfeited, and a throw-in is awarded to the opposing team at the exact same spot.

For goal-kicks, a corner kick is awarded to the opposing side.

3 319 set-piece goals were scored in the Premier League last season Credit: Getty

Premier League 26/27 opening fixtures 3pm kick-offs unless stated Friday, August 22 Arsenal vs Coventry - 8pm, live on talkSPORT Saturday, August 23 Hull vs Manchester United - 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT

Everton vs Crystal Palace

Ipswich vs Sunderland

Brentford vs Tottenham - 5.30pm Sunday, August 24 Brighton vs Aston Villa - 2pm

Manchester City vs Bournemouth - 2pm

Newcastle vs Liverpool - 4.30pm Monday, August 25 Fulham vs Chelsea - 8pm, live on talkSPORT

Why is the Premier League enforcing it?

Goalkeepers and defenders have often used routine restarts late in matches to disrupt the flow of play.

They often slowly walk to the ball or place it down multiple times to kill time.

Prior to the rule change, officials could only punish these tactics by issuing a yellow card.

It was a sanction players would willingly accept during injury time.

By threatening players with a counter-attacking opportunity, the PGMOL expects players to restart play far more quickly.

With set-piece goals proving crucial in the Premier League last season, taking five seconds too long over a goal-kick could prove the difference in securing three points this campaign.

The system was well integrated into the World Cup this summer, with players maintaining the usual flow of the game - even in high-stake moments.

However, some players appeared to have come up with a way around the new rule change, including Scotland's Andy Robertson.

3 Fans spotted Robertson's throw-in hack during Scotland's group stage win over Haiti Credit: Getty

The Tartan Army captain was spotted signalling his teammates into position before picking up the ball.

As a result, the referee did not start the countdown for him to take the throw-in, allowing his side extra time to reset while holding a 1-0 lead to Haiti.

The rule will also be enforced throughout English football in both the men's and women's game, including in the EFL, the WSL, and the National League.

Sports.title: New Premier League substitution rule could see players banned for entering pitch
Sports.content:
New Premier League substitution rule could see players banned for entering pitch

The Premier League is back and managers and players will need to navigate a host of major rule changes designed to stamp out time-wasting.

The PGMOL has confirmed a brand-new substitution law that could leave teams a player down.



3 No player received the sanction at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

Refereeing chiefs have made it their mission to speed up the game following the implementation of new regulations at the World Cup.

They want to target the tactical thinking of footballers taking slow, deliberate walks across the pitch when their number is raised on the board.

The new rule will only allow a strict 10-second time limit for substituted players to leave the pitch.



Failure to do so will force clubs to play with only ten men, and could prove disastrous for teams protecting a tight lead late on.

What is the Premier League's 10-second substitution rule?

Under the new law, a player being substituted has exactly ten seconds to completely leave the pitch once the electronic board is displayed by the fourth official.



Additionally, players must exit using the nearest point on the boundary line, unless directed otherwise by the match officials for safety or security reasons.

If a player takes longer than the allocated time to cross the touchline, their replacement is barred from entering the field for at least one minute.



Their team must play temporarily with a reduced side until the first natural stoppage after that minute has elapsed.

3 Michael Oliver will be used to the rule after refereeing at the summer tournament Credit: Getty

Why is the Premier League enforcing it?

For years, Premier League managers have used late substitutions to disrupt momentum and run down the clock.

Previously, referees could only punish slow exits by showing a yellow card to the departing player.



The old sanction rarely discouraged teams from employing the tactic late in matches.

By forcing a club to play with a man down for over a minute, the PGMOL expects players to sprint off the pitch to avoid leaving their teammates vulnerable.

Following the successful introduction of the measures at the World Cup during the summer, the FA was keen to adopt the set of rules for English football.

The rule will also be implemented across the men's and women's professional game in England, including the EFL, WSL Football and the National League



3 Goalkeepers are often accused of faking injury to waste time, but this trial is designed to stop that Credit: Getty

Premier League 26/27 opening fixtures 3pm kick-offs unless stated Friday, August 22 Arsenal vs Coventry - 8pm, live on talkSPORT Saturday, August 23 Hull vs Manchester United - 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT

Manchester City vs Bournemouth - 2pm

Newcastle vs Liverpool - 4.30pm Monday, August 25 Fulham vs Chelsea - 8pm, live on talkSPORT

What other rules have been introduced?

Goalkeepers will also be subjected to new regulations.

If play stops for a keeper injury, they must also leave the pitch upon restart like any other player - unless the stoppage involves a direct collision or is a serious issue.

Pro Ref released a statement saying: "The trial, championed collectively by Pro Ref, The FA, Premier League, EFL, WSL Football and the National League, will be implemented across the men's and women's professional game in England,

"And is designed to address occasions where goalkeeper injuries have been used to disrupt momentum, slow the game down or create opportunities for tactical instruction."



Meanwhile, any outfield player who receives on-pitch treatment must now remain off the field for a minimum of 60 seconds - doubled from the previous 30 seconds.

Additionally, referees will enforce a five-second countdown for throw-ins and goal-kicks, with a potential reversal of possession for delays.

VAR can now review second yellow card incidents, though a high threshold for intervention remains in place for other decisions.

There will also be increased focus on penalising holding in the box that materially impacts play.
